title: Days 271–284 runtime and SQL measurement foundations

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: 11.1. Introduction
sources.use: Compare indexed/unindexed access while holding query results fixed.

sources.title: statistics — Mathematical statistics functions — Python 3.12.15 documentation

days.title: Capture a deterministic SQL baseline
days.task: Run prior gates read-only and capture the baseline workload to a fresh ignored artifact path; leave the canonical fixture unchanged.
days.evidence: Gate outputs; artifact path; exact ordered rows; canonical fixture SHA before/after.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q17 — Cache: accelerate a read; follow-up: state which measured read path and freshness requirement would justify a cache.
days.architecture: Pin PostgreSQL 18.6 and deterministic seed data; bind only to loopback and capture to ignored target/ so fresh observations never overwrite the canonical fixture.
days.reserve_fallback_task: repeat the same baseline into a distinct artifact and compare complete row identities.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Second artifact path, identical expected/observed rows, unchanged canonical fixture digest.
days.study_task: Read the plan-tree basics; identify which result facts must be independently checked before interpreting a scan node.
days.study_evidence: One note separating query-result correctness from estimated plan cost/node choice.

days.title: Verify the workload's relational facts
days.task: Derive the expected owner/policy/revision list from the schema seed independently and compare it with Day271 rows; include a same-count foreign-owner example.
days.command: python3 -c 'import json; x=json.load(open("target/runtime-sql-lab/day271-observation.json")); expected=[{"owner_id":"owner-07","policy_id":"policy-0012","revision":r} for r in range(8,3,-1)]; print(expected == x["observed_rows"], expected)'
days.evidence: Independently derived ordered composite identities and same-count foreign-owner counterexample.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q18 — Cache: invalidation after a write; follow-up: include tenant change and stale-version denial.
days.architecture: Derive the expected composite identities from the seed arithmetic, independently of planner output; exact order and tenant keys prevent a same-count leak from passing.
days.reserve_fallback_task: derive the five expected revision numbers independently, then verify actual rows and order.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Expected revision list and hand-checked row identity/order.
days.study_task: Read how PostgreSQL indexes reduce candidate row search; identify when a sequential scan may still be reasonable.
days.study_evidence: One source-backed indexed-versus-sequential-scan note without claiming the index is always faster.

days.title: Implement exact result comparison
days.task: Implement complete ordered owner/policy/revision equality. Reject mutations to each key field and row order, even when count remains five.
days.evidence: Owner, policy, revision and reorder cases rejected by the actual acceptance path.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q13 — Booking: reserve one seat atomically; follow-up: reason about the final two concurrent requests.
days.architecture: Compare complete ordered composite identities; neither count-only nor order-insensitive checking can establish that the intended revisions were read.
days.reserve_fallback_task: run same-count owner, policy, revision and reordered row negatives through acceptance.
days.study_task: Read what EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes and returns; distinguish measured row counts from timing noise.
days.study_evidence: One source-backed distinction between actual row counts and elapsed time.

days.title: Compare estimated and actual cardinality
days.task: Implement finite estimate/actual q-error and explicit zero/zero versus zero/nonzero handling; inspect the 4x counterfactual.
days.evidence: Baseline arithmetic, 4x estimate negative control and explicit zero mismatch; no timing assertion.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q10 — Notification service: retries; follow-up: include a lost response after a worker timeout.
days.architecture: Use a symmetric finite ratio for nonzero counts and explicit zero states; avoid undefined division and do not turn q-error into a speed or correctness score.
days.reserve_fallback_task: rerun 4x, zero/zero and zero/nonzero q-error controls on deep-copied input.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Expected q-error 4.0 and zero-state outputs from copied inputs.
days.study_task: Read how single-column statistics inform estimates; note a case where correlated columns need more than a single-column histogram.
days.study_evidence: One source-backed estimate limitation tied to the observed query.

days.title: Apply the analyzer to a skewed workload
days.task: Run the skew experiment, pass its captured query observation through the learner analyzer built on Days273–274, and independently inspect nested owner-row estimates before/after ANALYZE.
days.command: scripts/capture_runtime_sql_fixture.sh target/runtime-sql-lab/day275-skew.json skew && python3 -c 'import json; from labs.runtime_sql.learner_analysis import analyze_observation; x=json.load(open("target/runtime-sql-lab/day275-skew.json")); print(analyze_observation(x))'
days.evidence: Learner analyzer reports complete expected rows and finite root metrics; expected/observed owner rows both 4,240; before/after EXPLAIN JSON; no required estimate delta.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q22 — Webhook delivery: backoff and dead letter; follow-up: state the terminal failure and safe replay behavior.
days.architecture: Add a known 4,000-row owner skew, capture before and after ANALYZE, then feed the unchanged policy query through the completed learner analyzer. Keep plan estimates observational: statistics refresh does not promise a particular node or estimate.
days.reserve_fallback_task: rerun skew capture, apply the learner analyzer to its policy query, and independently check actual owner count plus nested estimates before/after ANALYZE.
days.reserve_fallback_command: scripts/capture_runtime_sql_fixture.sh target/runtime-sql-lab/day275-skew.json skew && python3 -c 'import json; from labs.runtime_sql.learner_analysis import analyze_observation; x=json.load(open("target/runtime-sql-lab/day275-skew.json")); print(analyze_observation(x))' && python3 scripts/report_runtime_sql_skew.py target/runtime-sql-lab/day275-skew.json
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Analyzer output, independent 4,240 actual owner count, and both plan trees retained.
days.study_task: Read what ANALYZE collects and how the planner uses it; record why a new distribution can make old statistics stale.
days.study_evidence: One source-backed explanation of when ANALYZE changes a planner's information.

days.title: Validate malformed plan evidence
days.task: Implement fail-closed plan-field validation, then read both nested skew plans and compare estimated versus actual owner rows without assuming a specific node.
days.evidence: Missing/type/negative/NaN cases fail closed; reported nested estimates and actual 4,240 owner rows before/after.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q12 — Scheduler: missed or duplicate execution; follow-up: worker stops after claim and before completion.
days.architecture: Validate types and finite ranges before interpreting plan data; report nested scan estimates from the skew artifact without hard-coding a plan-tree shape or requiring statistics to improve estimates.
days.reserve_fallback_task: run malformed plan controls and independently inspect skew scan estimates plus exact actual count.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Malformed cases rejected and skew actual count independently confirmed.
days.study_task: Read the extended-statistics section and name which correlations it can capture and which workload facts remain unknown.
days.study_evidence: One short note on multicolumn correlation and limits of planner statistics.

days.title: Compare plan and answer independently
days.task: Drop the composite index in a fresh database; compare baseline and no-index runs through the result-preserving comparator.
days.evidence: Exact same ordered rows across variants; planner/buffer/timing values reported as observations, no speed threshold.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q24 — Event pipeline: correction and replay; follow-up: include a side effect already emitted by the old projection.
days.architecture: Use a fresh disposable database with only the index layout changed; the answer rows must stay exact while the plan/cost/buffers may differ.
days.reserve_fallback_task: repeat the no-index comparison, separating invariant answer rows from varied plan observations.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Comparator confirms identical complete rows and reports run-specific plan values.
days.study_task: Read the planner caveats; list data size, cache, statistics, and host factors that make a timing comparison noisy.
days.study_evidence: At least three caveats and one explicit non-claim for this experiment.

days.title: Record a bounded JVM profile
days.task: Compile the bounded 500-million-iteration CPU workload; record one JFR file and verify its deterministic checksum and custom phase event.
days.command: mkdir -p target/runtime-sql-lab/classes && javac -d target/runtime-sql-lab/classes labs/runtime_sql/ProfilingWork.java && java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork && jfr summary target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr
days.evidence: Exactly 500,000,000 iterations, checksum 7,954,362,999, file path, JDK version, phase marker and summary; bounded synthetic workload only.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q02 — Short-link abuse and operations; follow-up: separate a CPU signal from a traffic-abuse hypothesis.
days.architecture: Use a fixed 500-million-iteration CPU loop to provide a bounded sustained phase while keeping work identity deterministic. JFR defaults limit event volume; sampling and recording overhead remain variable, and this local loop is not a service profile.
days.reserve_fallback_task: repeat the fixed loop in a fresh process and inspect the deterministic marker/checksum plus local summary, not duration.
days.reserve_fallback_command: java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day278-reserve.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork && jfr print --events lab.WorkPhase target/runtime-sql-lab/day278-reserve.jfr && jfr summary target/runtime-sql-lab/day278-reserve.jfr
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: One marker with 500,000,000 iterations and checksum 7,954,362,999 plus summary; timing/sample counts retained as variable observations.
days.study_task: Read the JFR file/tool overview; identify one benefit and one cost of recording a short local process.
days.study_evidence: One benefit, one recording overhead/selection caveat, no service-profile claim.

days.title: Inspect selected recording events
days.task: Inspect the required lab.WorkPhase marker and JFR summary; validate workload, iteration count and checksum. Record ExecutionSample count as optional observed data, never as the sole success condition.
days.command: if [ ! -s target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr ] || [ ! -s target/runtime-sql-lab/classes/ProfilingWork.class ]; then mkdir -p target/runtime-sql-lab/classes && javac -d target/runtime-sql-lab/classes labs/runtime_sql/ProfilingWork.java && java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork; fi; jfr print --events lab.WorkPhase target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr && jfr summary target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr
days.evidence: Exactly one custom marker with cpu-bitcount-v1, 500M iterations and known checksum; inspect event fields and actual ExecutionSample count if present, no brittle count threshold.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q09 — Notification service: accept and deliver; follow-up: provider unavailable after durable intent is recorded.
days.architecture: Use an enabled custom JFR phase event as a deterministic recording-integrity marker; inspect its workload fields and summary, then report sampled ExecutionSample data separately because counts vary with host and sampling intervals.
days.reserve_fallback_task: recreate the recording if missing, then verify the phase marker fields and record any sample count shown by summary.
days.reserve_fallback_command: mkdir -p target/runtime-sql-lab/classes && javac -d target/runtime-sql-lab/classes labs/runtime_sql/ProfilingWork.java && java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork && jfr print --events lab.WorkPhase target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr && jfr summary target/runtime-sql-lab/day278.jfr
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: One valid 500M marker with expected checksum; actual optional ExecutionSample count retained.
days.study_task: Read the Event API lifecycle; distinguish a deliberate phase marker from sampled execution events.
days.study_evidence: One note on marker duration/fields and why sampled counts may vary.

days.title: Relate runtime observations to workload
days.task: Create two fresh JFR recordings from the same workload, inspect both custom phase markers and summaries, and compare checksums rather than exact sample counts.
days.command: mkdir -p target/runtime-sql-lab/classes && javac -d target/runtime-sql-lab/classes labs/runtime_sql/ProfilingWork.java && for n in 1 2; do java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day280-$n.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork && jfr print --events lab.WorkPhase target/runtime-sql-lab/day280-$n.jfr && jfr summary target/runtime-sql-lab/day280-$n.jfr; done
days.evidence: Two markers with identical 500,000,000-iteration workload/checksum values; differing sample counts documented, no exact event count requirement.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q35 — Distributed rate limiting; follow-up: one region partitioned and fairness is required.
days.architecture: Use separate JVMs and recordings so samples do not share process state; require identical 500M custom markers and checksums, allow sampled event counts to differ, and avoid comparing wall-clock duration.
days.reserve_fallback_task: if either recording is absent recreate both; compare each custom marker's workload and checksum.
days.reserve_fallback_command: mkdir -p target/runtime-sql-lab/classes && javac -d target/runtime-sql-lab/classes labs/runtime_sql/ProfilingWork.java && for n in 1 2; do java -XX:StartFlightRecording=filename=target/runtime-sql-lab/day280-$n.jfr,dumponexit=true -cp target/runtime-sql-lab/classes ProfilingWork && jfr print --events lab.WorkPhase target/runtime-sql-lab/day280-$n.jfr; done
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Two 500M marker records with the same expected checksum; sample variation retained as observation.
days.study_task: Read the summary command output and separate recorder metadata from event evidence.
days.study_evidence: List which summary fields establish recording existence and which do not establish profile quality.

days.title: Re-run acceptance mutations
days.task: Run independent oracle plus actual acceptance-path mutations for owner, policy, revision, order, missing/extra/same-count substitution, q-error, buffers and malformed evidence.
days.evidence: Reference passes and every named faulty comparator/metric mutation is rejected; learner TODO remains uncredited.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q34 — Analytics: late and duplicate data; follow-up: replay a duplicate after a correction.
days.architecture: The instructor reference remains isolated from the learner starter; independent expected facts and mutations protect the real assertion path without awarding learner credit.
days.reserve_fallback_task: rerun the actual-path mutation matrix and retain the failing assertion for each faulty comparator.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Actual assertion failures for row, q-error, buffer and malformed-input mutants.
days.study_task: Read the leading-column discussion and relate exact ordered composite identity checks to the limits of index-order conclusions.
days.study_evidence: One note separating result identity from workload-specific index performance.

days.title: Explain a planner counterfactual
days.task: Recreate the query with reversed composite-index order and compare against baseline; verify full result identity despite plan differences.
days.evidence: Exact same rows and reported per-variant plan/counters; no claim that either ordering is universally faster.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q27 — Feed: build a page; follow-up: new items arrive between pages and cursor stability matters.
days.architecture: Change only multicolumn key order in a clean database and keep the exact query/result fixed; both equality predicates are present, so conclusions remain workload-specific.
days.reserve_fallback_task: rerun the reverse-index capture and compare full rows and observed plan fields to the baseline.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Complete row equality plus unchanged/changed plan observations, without a preferred index claim.
days.study_task: Read the leading-column discussion; predict what changes and what must remain invariant when the index order changes.
days.study_evidence: One prediction and a falsifying outcome for this two-equality synthetic query.

days.title: Reproduce and compare the observation
days.task: Capture another baseline in a fresh container and use the comparator to verify exact rows against Day271; note which plan/buffer values vary.
days.evidence: Exact ordered result equality, per-run planner and buffer observations, canonical fixture unchanged.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q32 — Streaming: adaptive delivery; follow-up: compare throughput and buffering under one regional failure.
days.architecture: Rebuild the same seed and ANALYZE state in a fresh instance; correctness must transfer while volatile planner/cache observations are reported, not normalized away.
days.reserve_fallback_task: capture one more baseline and compare exact rows with both Day271 and Day283 artifacts.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Fresh artifact, exact rows and run-specific volatile fields.
days.study_task: Review why each clean fixture recomputes planner statistics and what that does not control (host/cache effects).
days.study_evidence: One statement separating ANALYZE reproducibility from timing reproducibility.

days.title: Review gates and transfer the diagnosis
days.task: Capture a third baseline run, summarize actual execution-time center/spread with the provided script, run independent lab acceptance, and record separate dynamic gate outputs/carry-forward.
days.command: scripts/capture_runtime_sql_fixture.sh target/runtime-sql-lab/day284-observation.json baseline && python3 scripts/summarize_runtime_sql_runs.py target/runtime-sql-lab/day271-observation.json target/runtime-sql-lab/day283-observation.json target/runtime-sql-lab/day284-observation.json && python3 -m unittest scripts.test_continuation_271_284
days.evidence: Three baseline captures with identical full expected rows; actual median/spread output and limitations; lab acceptance output. Run historical gates separately and retain their raw result; gates do not short-circuit lab checks.
days.shared_task: Question bank Q36 — Object-store recovery; follow-up: verify a restored object's checksum after accidental deletion.
days.architecture: Keep the same baseline variant and exact answer across three fresh local runs; summarize median and spread to teach Python statistics, but treat tiny same-host timings as descriptive, not a service SLO.
days.reserve_fallback_task: if a baseline capture is missing, recreate it; then run each prior gate independently and record the next actual recovery selector.
days.reserve_fallback_evidence: Three same-variant captures or exact missing capture selector; raw gate outputs; no eligibility/completion inference.
days.study_task: Use Python statistics.median and statistics.pstdev on three same-variant PostgreSQL actual-time observations; explain why n=3 on one host is descriptive only.
days.study_evidence: Median, population standard deviation, min/max, n=3, and a written limitation; no performance pass/fail.
